title: P19 reversed, second step: raise the wall-clock cosine learning-rate floor from 0.3 to 0.5 of peak (AdamW and Muon) on the 129-claude hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (4,800,000 params)
description: P19 reversed (P18/P19 schedule family): MIN_LR_FRAC 0.3 -> 0.5 is the only edit, so the handoff LR is half of peak instead of 0.3 and the cosine never goes below 0.5x peak (129 is below 0.5x for the last ~36% of the 300 s budget). 129 (0.1 -> 0.3, +15, every seed up) showed a less-annealed handoff samples worse in round 1 but climbs faster under expert iteration, and 130 (no decay, -63) showed the undecayed extreme is too noisy; this measures the untested middle of that curve, which both 129's and 130's write-ups named as the next point.
hypothesis: The fixed RL AdamW fine-tune gains more from a plastic, less-annealed start than it loses from a noisier round-1 sampler, up to a point: 129 traded -75 round-1 targets for +94 more r1->r4 growth and ended +15 on eval. If the metric vs floor curve (0.1: 631, 0.3: 646, constant: 583) is concave with its peak between 0.3 and 1.0, floor 0.5 keeps enough of the late cosine (LR still falls 2x from peak over the run) to avoid 130's round-1 collapse (greedy 0.82-0.91, up to 76% parse failures) while the higher endpoint gives RL an even more plastic start. Failure mode: 135's reading that round-1 harvest tracks time spent at low LR dominates, round 1 drops further (targets ~560-620 vs 647/610/684) and RL does not catch up, as in 130 and 135.
expected_delta: -5 central (range -45..+30) theorems at >=7 vs 129-claude's 646.33 mean. Pretraining predictions: steps ~4150-4250 (unchanged), final train loss ~0.055-0.058 (129 ~0.054), final val loss 0.078-0.090, held-out greedy 0.93-0.965 (129: 0.955-0.964), round-1 Lean parse failures 30-55% (129: 26-40%), round-1 targets 560-680, r1->r4 growth above 129's +478 mean.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and hybrid attention heads, ALiBi on 4 heads and no positional signal on the other 4 (P34 x P32); architecture unchanged from 115-fable
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: none vs 129-claude; the only edit is optimizer.min_lr_frac 0.3 -> 0.5
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 129-claude, 115-fable, 113-fable and 107-claude: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py (its ALIBI_SLOPES = (1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256, 0, 0, 0, 0)), replace blocks with PeriLNBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state (same keys as 107/113). Loading these weights into 113's model (slopes 1/2..1/256) or a plain fork GPT (RoPE) gives a different function. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged from 129-claude/115-fable (caches[0] holds key positions; slope-0 heads get a zero bias plus the -inf mask); this patch does not touch model code

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with CHANGED floor: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.5 + 0.25 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.5 x peak (129-claude: 0.3 x peak; 115-fable: 0.1 x peak). Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 follows the same factor, and so does its per-step decoupled decay lr * MUON_WD

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor CHANGED 0.3 -> 0.5); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 5/3 x 129's, 5x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
